I added a PR to *ttls* to get basic playlist (and predefined effects) support.

https://github.com/jschlyter/ttls/pull/23
That will at least allow you to check if a playlist is defined.

With ttls 1.6.1 `get_playlist()` is available, and you can at least check if a playlist is available.
That would improve the PR.

Whether frenck has changed his mind about the implementation is another case.

> > Considering this, I don't think this should be mixed with the effects; it is especially odd to pull in a single mode into the effect list.
> 
> I agree. But to be honest, not all of these are relevant.
> 
> * Color is a static color, that is fine.
> * Demo is probably not very interesting for most users
> * Effect is just setting one of a predefined list of effects (possibly the same ones that are used in Demo mode?)  These don't have names, and I don't think an official list of these effects and their IDs are available. You are probably better off using Movies.
> * Movie is what I would call "effects" but must be added from the app to upload it to the device before they can be used.
> * Off is ... off.
> * Then there is Playlist.
> * RT is sending "frames" real time to the device.  Unless someone either creates a tool to compete with the mobile app to create these frames, or someone wants to hand code thousands of messages, this is also probably not going to be used from HA.
> 
> So from that list, only _color_, _movie_ and _playlist_ are probably relevant. Pluss maybe "effect" if someone can find an authoritative list of the preinstalled effects and give them some useful names. But that would just be added to the Effect-list anyway, and we would need a way to find out if it is a preinstalled _effect_ or a _movie_ when the user selects it.

I agree with the points you made.  I'm not in favor of playlist being chosen in a separate mode selector. As it currently stands, you can select effects when in color mode, or colors when in effect mode. Should we hide the color selector when in effect mode, or hide the effect list when in color mode? I don't think so, so why have playlist mode separate as well? I think it fits in nicely in the effect list, as it is a list of effects. Also, I didn't know that twinkly came with built in effects. If mine does, they aren't visible in the twinkly app.
 
Something I do think would be a nice addition is a separate default mode selector. [This comment](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/73336#issuecomment-1330815306) that sets playlist mode to default was well received. There are definitely people out there that want their twinkly to play a playlist when it turns on, and I'm sure others that want it on a color, or want it on an effect. 

As far as checking for a playlist, I could probably make that work but I am definitely not a python programmer. @Olen I think you would be much better suited to write something that is up to home assistant's standards (not telling you to do anything, just saying you certainly wouldn't be stepping on my toes.)

Did a quick and dirty implementation now, and it seems to work fine.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/203184/206471906-ce4f8ae5-cbb8-40cd-b57e-50aa9e1fb18b.png)

It sort of makes sense to have "Playlist" as an option in the dropdown, as you cant have _both_ an effect going _and_ a playlist running at the same time.  But you obviously want to be able to switch between running the playlist and selecting a specific effect.
I have a feeling the lighting season will be over before this gets resolved. See you in the next year.

@tannerwastaken 

I made your script multi-entity so they would be in sync with each other 

```

entity_ids = data.get("entity_ids")  # Pass a list of entities
current_effects = []

# Gather effects from all devices
for entity_id in entity_ids:
    state = hass.states.get(entity_id)
    current_effect_str = state.attributes.get("effect", "0").split(" ")[0]
    current_effects.append(int(current_effect_str))

# Assume all devices share the same current effect or just use the first
# If you want them perfectly synced, rely on the first device or find the minimum/maximum.
current_effect = current_effects[0]

# Determine the next effect (assuming all need to advance in sync)
next_effect = (current_effect + 1) % 13

logger.info("Next effect for all devices: %d", next_effect)

# Apply the next effect to all devices
for entity_id in entity_ids:
    service_data = {"entity_id": entity_id, "effect": str(next_effect)}
    hass.services.call("light", "turn_on", service_data, blocking=True)
```

review_comments:
Shouldn't this me a mode switch or select entity instead? 
I feel like this is misusing effects to trigger a playlist mode.
I'm not sure if this is the best way or not. A playlist is a list of effects, so I can see it being available in effects. It is essentially "all effects".
I'm expecting some Twinkly products to be delivered any moment now, so I'll await that an see how it would generally fit compared to other integrations.

I agree that this might not be the best way, but I don't know what would be the best way.  Possibly, "Playlist" (and maybe "Music") should be added to `class LightEntityFeature(IntFlag):` in the general light component.  But then one would also need to have ways to handle those in the UI and service calls.

Anyway, you should also check if a playlist is actually created before adding this. Currently get_playlist is not in ttls:
https://github.com/jschlyter/ttls/blob/main/ttls/client.py
https://xled-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rest_api.html#get-playlist

But [jschlyter](https://github.com/jschlyter) seems to be pretty responsive, so it should hopefully be an easy fix.


Another option is to create some Twinkly specific service calls like `twinkly_set_mode("playlist")` but I don't like that either.

A related problem I have seen in the GUI is that if you are using an effect, and then select a static color, and then want to go back to the effect you previously used, you need to first select another effect. Ok, so it seems like a Twinkly device can be in all kinds of modes:

- `color`
- `demo`
- `effect`
- `movie`
- `off`
- `playlist`
- `rt`

Considering this, I don't think this should be mixed with the effects; it is especially odd to pull in a single mode into the effect list.

Besides that, music mode could be enabled too which is not part of the default "modes" but more a separate functionality - with a confusing name - that can be applied with (some) effects, so that probably deserves its own dedicated switch entity.

It's not an issue. That can be created, we have `select` entities for that purpose.

> Considering this, I don't think this should be mixed with the effects; it is especially odd to pull in a single mode into the effect list.

I agree. But to be honest, not all of these are relevant. 
* Color is a static color, that is fine.
* Demo is probably not very interesting for most users
* Effect is just setting one of a predefined list of effects (possibly the same ones that are used in Demo mode?)  These don't have names, and I don't think an official list of these effects and their IDs are available. You are probably better off using Movies.
* Movie is what I would call "effects" but must be added from the app to upload it to the device before they can be used.
* Off is ... off.
* Then there is Playlist.
* RT is sending "frames" real time to the device.  Unless someone either creates a tool to compete with the mobile app to create these frames, or someone wants to hand code thousands of messages, this is also probably not going to be used from HA.

So from that list, only *color*, *movie* and *playlist* are probably relevant. Pluss maybe "effect" if someone can find an authoritative list of the preinstalled effects and give them some useful names. But that would just be added to the Effect-list anyway, and we would need a way to find out if it is a preinstalled *effect* or a *movie* when the user selects it.
